## Conclusion

The warning is caused by a **USB Type-C connector teardown race**, not by a UCSI protocol error or a Dell-specific firmware-created missing directory.

The stale state is created in `drivers/usb/core/port.c::connector_unbind()`: it clears `port_dev->connector` without first calling `typec_deattach()`. Consequently, the Type-C class retains `port->usb2_dev`/`port->usb3_dev` after the USB device's sysfs kobject has begun teardown. Later, UCSI unregisters the partner and tries to remove the already-detached device-side `typec` symlink.

The upstream fix exists, but it is **not present in this tree**.

---

## 1. UCSI call chain

In this tree:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  -> ucsi_unregister_partner()
     -> typec_unregister_partner()
```

Evidence:

- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264` — `ucsi_handle_connector_change()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1306-1326` — processes `UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1325` — disconnect path calls:

```c
ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
```

- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138-1154` — `ucsi_unregister_partner()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1151` — calls:

```c
typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
```

The relevant code is:

```c
static void ucsi_unregister_partner(struct ucsi_connector *con)
{
	if (!con->partner)
		return;

	typec_set_mode(con->port, TYPEC_STATE_SAFE);
	...
	typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
	...
	con->partner = NULL;
}
```

Thus the reported stack is consistent with the normal UCSI disconnect path.

---

## 2. Type-C partner teardown

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174-1196` contains `typec_unregister_partner()`:

```c
mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
if (port->usb2_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
	port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}

device_unregister(&partner->dev);
mutex_unlock(&port->partner_link_lock);
```

The important helper is `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
					struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");

	if (partner->deattach)
		partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

The warning concerns the second removal:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
```

The `typec` link is created on the USB device by `typec_partner_link_device()` at `drivers/usb/usb/typec/class.c:890-904`:

```c
sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

The Type-C class stores the enumerated USB device in:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2146-2167`, `typec_partner_attach()`
- `port->usb2_dev = dev` or `port->usb3_dev = dev`

The corresponding detach callback is:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2169-2186`, `typec_partner_deattach()`
- installed at `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2753`:

```c
port->con.deattach = typec_partner_deattach;
```

`typec_partner_deattach()` removes the Type-C link and clears the cached USB-device pointer:

```c
if (partner) {
	typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev);
	put_device(&partner->dev);
}

if (port->usb2_dev == dev)
	port->usb2_dev = NULL;
else if (port->usb3_dev == dev)
	port->usb3_dev = NULL;
```

---

## 3. Root cause: `connector_unbind()` fails to detach the Type-C device

The USB component binding path is in `drivers/usb/core/port.c`.

`connector_bind()` at `port.c:695-720` does the expected Type-C attach:

```c
port_dev->connector = data;

if (port_dev->child)
	typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
```

However, `connector_unbind()` at `port.c:722-729` currently does this:

```c
static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector,
			     void *data)
{
	struct usb_port *port_dev = to_usb_port(dev);

	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
}
```

It removes the component links and immediately clears `port_dev->connector`, but it does **not** call:

```c
typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
```

That omission leaves the Type-C class's cached `port->usb2_dev` or `port->usb3_dev` pointing at the USB device.

Later, `usb_disconnect()` in `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363` attempts:

```c
typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &udev->dev);
```

But `connector_unbind()` has already set `port_dev->connector = NULL`, so the inline helper in `include/linux/usb/typec.h:410-414` does nothing:

```c
static inline void typec_deattach(struct typec_connector *con,
				  struct device *dev)
{
	if (con && con->deattach)
		con->deattach(con, dev);
}
```

Therefore `typec_partner_deattach()` is never called, and the Type-C class retains the stale USB-device pointer.

The later UCSI work item then reaches `typec_unregister_partner()`, which reads that stale pointer and calls `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")`.

---

## 4. Why kernfs says “no directory”

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:909` calls:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
```

`fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-155` obtains the kobject's kernfs directory:

```c
if (!kobj)
	parent = sysfs_root_kn;
else
	parent = kobj->sd;

kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
```

The USB device is already being removed or has had its sysfs representation detached. Therefore `dev->kobj.sd` can be `NULL`.

`kernfs_remove_by_name()` resolves to `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`, whose implementation is in `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724-1752`:

```c
if (!parent) {
	WARN(1, KERN_WARNING
	     "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
	return -ENOENT;
}
```

Hence:

```text
kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
```

means that the parent kernfs directory passed to the removal operation is already gone. It is not merely the ordinary “symlink name was absent” case: the warning specifically comes from the `!parent` branch.

The complete chain is:

```text
connector_unbind()
  port.c:722-729
    port_dev->connector = NULL
    [missing typec_deattach()]

usb device teardown
  hub.c:2363
    typec_deattach(NULL, &udev->dev)
    [no-op]

UCSI disconnect work
  ucsi.c:1264
    ucsi_unregister_partner()
      ucsi.c:1325 / 1138-1154
        typec_unregister_partner()
          class.c:1185/1189
            typec_partner_unlink_device()
              class.c:909
                sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")
                  kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
                    WARN(... "no directory")
```

---

## 5. Is the fix present in this tree?

### The locking fix is present

This tree already contains the earlier Type-C locking fix:

```text
ec27386de23a511008c53aa2f3434ad180a3ca9a
usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access
```

Its changes are reflected here:

- `partner_link_lock` is initialized at `class.c:2748`
- `typec_partner_attach()` locks it at `class.c:2139`
- `typec_partner_deattach()` locks it at `class.c:2174`
- `typec_unregister_partner()` locks it at `class.c:1183`

That fix prevents concurrent manipulation of the cached USB-device pointers, but it does not repair the missing detach in `connector_unbind()`.

### The relevant race fix is absent

The upstream fix is:

```text
e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a
usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
```

It adds to `drivers/usb/core/port.c::connector_unbind()`:

```c
if (port_dev->child)
	typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
```

before:

```c
port_dev->connector = NULL;
```

The corrected ordering is therefore:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");

if (port_dev->child)
```

## Final assessment

- **Root cause:** missing `typec_deattach()` in `drivers/usb/core/port.c::connector_unbind()`.
- **Offending Type-C functions:** `typec_partner_attach()`, `typec_partner_deattach()`, `typec_partner_unlink_device()`, and `typec_unregister_partner()` in `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`.
